hero.headline: Print the QR once. Change the menu forever.
hero.subheadline: Your menu lives online and the QR code holds only a short permanent link. Change a price at 11pm and the table tents are already right — no reprinting, no stickers, no new codes.

problem.title: Why most QR menus need reprinting
problem.body: Free QR menu tools pack your whole menu inside the QR image itself. It is a neat trick — no hosting, nothing to expire — but it means the code is the menu. Change one price and you get a different code, so every table tent, counter sticker and delivery bag has to be redone. It also caps you at roughly 2,900 characters, about 60–100 dishes.
problem.resolution: Setu QR Menu turns that around. The code points to a permanent link, and the menu behind it is yours to change whenever you like.

features.title: One permanent code
features.description: Your link is fixed at signup and can never change. Print it on table tents, menus and packaging once and never think about it again.

features.title: Change prices instantly
features.description: Edit a price and it reaches the next diner who scans. No republish step, no waiting, no reprint.

features.title: Sold-out toggles
features.description: Ran out of prawns? Flip a switch and the dish shows as sold out instead of disappointing someone at the table.

features.title: Sizes and variations

features.title: Your brand

trust.title: The things people check before they order
trust.subtitle: A menu is not only prices. For someone who has never eaten with you, it is the thing they use to decide whether to trust you at all.

items.title: Your hygiene grade, beside your name
items.description: Show your official grade — A, B, C or D — right next to the business name, where someone deciding whether to order will actually see it.

items.title: The certificate, one tap away
items.description: Upload the certificate as an image or a PDF and a diner can open the document itself, instead of taking your word for the letter.

items.title: A pinned notice at the top
items.description: GST extra. 5% service charge. Kitchen closes at 10:30. Put it where it gets read before the order rather than argued about after the bill.

items.title: Opening hours with a live badge
items.description: Set your hours for each day and the menu works out whether you are open, showing an Open now badge on its own. Fewer calls asking.

items.title: A gallery of up to twelve photos
items.description: The room, the counter, the tandoor, the plates. Photos that do not belong to any one dish get a gallery of their own.

items.title: An About Us page behind the menu
items.description: Who you are, who cooks, what year you opened. One tap from the menu, for the diners who want to know before they order.

depth.title: A dish is more than a name and a price
depth.subtitle: Sizes and variations are where most menus stop. This is what sits underneath them.

items.title: Add-on pricing
items.description: Options that add to the dish price instead of replacing it. Extra cheese +₹40, add a scoop +₹30 — the diner sees what it comes to.

items.title: Pick-several option groups
items.description: Toppings, sides, spice level. Some groups take a single choice, others take as many as the diner wants — you decide that per group.

items.title: Up to three labels a dish
items.description: Bestseller, Chef's special, Spicy, New. Up to three labels per dish, each with its own icon, so the menu points somewhere instead of lying flat.

items.title: Veg and non-veg marks
items.description: The green and brown marks Indian diners look for first, drawn the way the FSSAI convention expects. On a menu in India this is not decoration.

items.title: Excel that survives the round trip
items.description: Export to Excel, change a hundred prices in a spreadsheet, import it back. Variations and labels come back intact rather than flattened into plain rows.

brand.title: Three templates, your colours, eleven kinds of business

items.title: Eight colours you can edit
items.description: Each template gives you eight editable colour tokens, not one brand colour stretched over everything. Match your signage properly instead of getting close.

items.title: A banner behind the menu header
items.description: Your room, your counter or your best plate sits behind the header. It is the first thing anyone sees in the second after the scan.

items.title: Cuisine chips under your name
items.description: North Indian, Chinese, Bakery. Small chips under the business name tell a diner what to expect before they scroll a single category.

items.title: Not only restaurants
items.description: Eleven business types to choose from, salons, spas and retail shops included. Pick yours and the menu reads like your price list, not someone else's food menu.

diner.title: What the person holding the phone gets
diner.subtitle: Everything above is for you. This is the menu your diner actually holds.

items.title: Search across the whole menu
items.description: Type paneer and get every match, in names and descriptions alike. On a long menu that is the difference between ordering and giving up.

items.title: A price calculator on every dish
items.description: A quantity stepper on the dish, with the total worked out as it goes. Handy for a table of six, and for anyone keeping an eye on the bill.

items.title: A recommendations carousel
items.description: The dishes you want ordered, in a swipeable row at the top of the menu, in front of everyone who scans.

items.title: Favourites, kept on their own phone
items.description: A regular marks what they always order and it is there next time. Stored on their device, with no account to make and nothing for you to hold.

items.title: An address that opens Maps
items.description: Tap the address and Google Maps or Apple Maps opens with directions. The shortest route from a forwarded menu link to someone walking in.

items.title: A link to your reviews
items.description: Send a happy diner to the place where a review counts, while the meal is still in front of them rather than three days later.

items.title: A share sheet
items.description: Diners forward the menu to whoever is joining them. Your menu travels on WhatsApp without you having to send anything.

operator.title: Built for the day your menu hits a hundred dishes
operator.subtitle: Nobody wants to scroll a hundred open forms to change one price.

items.title: Dish rows fold to one line
items.description: Every dish collapses to a summary line — name, price, status. Open only the one you came to change.

items.title: Collapsible categories
items.description: Fold a category away, or expand and collapse the whole menu in a click.

items.title: Search and filter while editing
items.description: Find a dish by name or narrow the editor to one category instead of hunting down the page.

items.title: Duplicate a menu to draft safely
items.description: Copy the live menu, rework the copy at your own pace, switch when it is ready. Nobody scanning sees the draft.

items.title: Live preview beside the editor
items.description: The diner's view sits next to the form and moves as you type. No publish-and-check loop.

items.title: Choose what gets recommended
items.description: Pick the category that feeds the recommendations carousel, so the dishes you push are the ones you chose.

items.title: It tells you when a save fails
items.description: If a setting does not reach the server you are told about it. Silence is never treated as success.

items.title: Your grading authority, your wording
items.description: MCD, FSSAI, BMC or whoever grades you — set the issuing authority so the badge on your menu says the right thing.

items.title: The grade retires itself
items.description: Give the certificate its expiry date and the grade leaves the menu when it lapses. A stale grade on display is worse than no grade.

items.title: Password reset by OTP
items.description: Locked out at nine on a Saturday? A one-time code to your email gets you back into the editor.

faq.question: What happens to my QR code when I change the menu?
faq.answer: Nothing — that is the whole point. The code carries a short permanent link, not the menu, so editing prices, adding dishes or switching to a different menu leaves it untouched. Print once and never reprint.

faq.question: How is this different from the free QR menu generator?
faq.answer: The free tool stores your entire menu inside the QR image, so a new code is produced every time you edit, and the menu is capped at roughly 2,900 characters. Here the menu is stored online, so the code stays fixed, there is no size limit, and you get photos, variations, sold-out toggles, multiple menus and scan analytics.

faq.question: Can I move my menu over from the free tool?
faq.answer: Yes. Paste the menu link from the free tool and every dish comes across, along with your tagline, phone number, address and brand colour. You can also import an Excel or CSV sheet.

faq.question: Can I show my hygiene grade on the menu?
faq.answer: Yes. Your official grade — A, B, C or D — sits beside your business name, and you can upload the certificate itself as an image or a PDF for diners to open. Set the issuing authority to whoever grades you, MCD, FSSAI, BMC or another, and give the certificate its expiry date: the grade takes itself off the menu when it lapses, so an out-of-date grade is never on display.

faq.question: Is this only for restaurants?
faq.answer: No. There are eleven business types to choose from, including salons, spas and retail shops. Pick yours and the menu presents itself as your price list rather than as a food menu — same permanent QR code, same editor, same photos and variations.

faq.question: Can I make the menu look like my brand?
faq.answer: Three templates — Classic, Bistro and Trattoria — each with eight colour tokens you can edit, so you match your signage rather than approximating it with a single accent colour. Add a banner image behind the menu header, your logo, and cuisine chips under your business name.

faq.question: What does a diner get besides the list of dishes?
faq.answer: Search across every dish name and description, a quantity stepper on each dish that totals as they go, a recommendations carousel, favourites saved on their own phone with no account, an address that opens Google or Apple Maps, a link to your reviews, and a share sheet so they can forward the menu to whoever is joining them.

faq.question: Do my customers need an app?
faq.answer: No. Any phone camera opens the menu in the browser. The page is deliberately light so it loads fast on a weak connection.

faq.question: Can I change my menu link later?
faq.answer: No, and that is deliberate. The link is what every printed QR code points to, so allowing it to change would silently break signage you have already paid to print. Everything else — your name, logo, colour, currency, dishes — can be changed freely.

faq.question: Is it really free for a year?
faq.answer: Yes. Sign up now and premium costs nothing for twelve months — every feature included, no card required, and nothing charged when the year ends unless you choose to continue. We will email you well before that date.

faq.question: What happens when the free year ends?
faq.answer: Your menu keeps being served, so printed QR codes carry on working. Editing pauses until you subscribe, and your data is kept exactly as it was, so continuing brings everything back on the same permanent link.
